title: Call, Zoom, Oct 13, 10:00 AM

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Okay, let's start. Thanks both for making time. Today is the Harbor app launch plan: the beta date, the pricing page, and who does what before the 14th.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: Sounds good. Quick context: Marisol from support says beta testers are happy with the new booking flow, but three of them reported the calendar sync failing on Android.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Right. Rafael, do you know what's behind the Android sync bug?

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: Yes, it's the token refresh. Android drops the refresh token when the phone is idle for an hour. I have a fix, it's about two days of work plus testing.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Two days is fine. Can that land before the beta opens?

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: If I start tomorrow, yes. I can have it ready by Wednesday, October 22.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: Then I'd suggest we open the beta on Monday, October 27. That gives support a full weekday of overlap with the fix.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: I like that. Any objection to October 27?

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: No objection from me, as long as QA signs off on Wednesday's build.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Okay, decision: the beta opens Monday, October 27, provided QA signs off on the Android fix.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: Good. Next, the pricing page. Right now it shows three plans, Free, Plus at nine dollars, and Team at twenty-nine.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Marisol told me the testers found Plus and Team confusing. Several asked what the difference was.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: I agree. I'd cut it down to two plans for the beta: Free and Plus, and hold Team back until we have shared calendars.

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: Shared calendars won't be ready until January at the earliest, so that makes sense.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: So we drop the Team plan from the beta page. Dana, is nine dollars still the right price for Plus?

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: My name is Elena, by the way, but yes. Nine dollars tested well in the survey. Seventy percent of respondents said they'd pay it.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Sorry, Elena, my mistake. Okay, decision: two plans in the beta, Free and Plus at nine dollars a month, Team comes back in January.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: Agreed. I'll rewrite the pricing page copy and send it to you for review by Friday, October 17.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll review it the same day so we don't slip.

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: One thing on my side: the App Store review. Apple usually takes about two days, sometimes five.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Then we should submit the iOS build early. Rafael, can you submit by Thursday, October 23?

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: Yes, but only if the Android fix doesn't block the shared code. I'll submit the iOS build on the twenty-third regardless and send Android right after.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: Okay. And for the launch emails, I'd like to schedule them through the new tool, but I haven't tested it.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Elena, can you run a test send to the three of us by next Tuesday, October 21?

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: Sure. I'll send a test email to everyone on Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: Can I raise a risk? The server load. If the beta gets a thousand sign-ups on day one, our current database plan may not hold.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: How many sign-ups are we expecting?

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: Marketing said between five hundred and two thousand. I honestly don't know. I'd like to load test before the twenty-seventh.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: Do we have budget for a bigger database plan if the load test fails?

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: I don't know yet. That's an open question: whether we can afford the larger database tier if the load test fails. I'll ask Chen in finance and we'll revisit on Friday.

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: Okay. I'll run the load test on Monday, October 20, and share the numbers with you both.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: One more item: the support macros. Marisol needs the new FAQ answers before the beta.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: I'll write the FAQ answers myself and give them to Marisol by Wednesday, October 22.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: Great. Should we also announce the beta on social media?

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Let's hold off. Decision: no public announcement until the Android fix is confirmed. We only email the waitlist on the twenty-seventh.

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: Makes sense. Less noise if something goes wrong.

transcript.speaker: them:0
transcript.text: So to recap: Rafael fixes Android by the twenty-second and runs the load test on the twentieth, I do the pricing copy by the seventeenth and the test email on the twenty-first.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: And I review the pricing copy on the seventeenth, write the FAQ by the twenty-second, and ask Chen about the budget.

transcript.speaker: them:1
transcript.text: And I submit iOS on the twenty-third. That's everything for me.

transcript.speaker: me
transcript.text: Great. Thanks, everyone. Let's meet again on Friday to look at the load test results.

decisions: Beta opens Monday Oct 27, if QA signs off the Android fix
Two plans in the beta: Free and Plus ($9/month); Team returns in January
No public announcement until the Android fix is confirmed; email the waitlist on the 27th
action_items: Submit iOS build to App Store
Ask Chen in finance about the database budget
